articleHeadline: What is scrub typhus
articleSummary: Death of a Government Kilpauk Medical College Hospital student in Chennai on Sept 18, 2026 from scrub typhus highlights its burden; Anna University has begun screening students for scrub typhus alongside dengue and leptospirosis. Scrub typhus is caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi and transmitted by chiggers, not mosquitoes. It is now the most common infectious cause of acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) in southern India, supported by a 2025 study of 587 children from Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. A 2021 systematic review found scrub typhus accounted for 25.3% of AUFI and community seroprevalence of 34.2%. Symptoms appear within about 10 days and include fever, chills, headache, body aches, eschar, mental changes, lymphadenopathy, and rash. Diagnosis via IgM ELISA or PCR; treatment with doxycycline or azithromycin—combination therapy reduced complications versus monotherapy (NEJM 2023). No vaccine; prevention focuses on avoiding chigger bites and reducing habitats; early diagnosis reduces mortality; surveillance needed.

articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) in Africa has reached over 120,000 cases and about 1,500 deaths from 2024–2026. articleSummary: Monkeypox (mpox) misdiagnoses in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) are highlighted by a University of Geneva study, in collaboration with WHO. articleHeadline: Multiplex LAMP-LFA for rapid field-compatible detection of environmental DNA from Schistosoma japonicum and Oncomelania hupensis quadrasi
articleSummary: Multiplex LAMP-LFA enables simultaneous detection of Schistosoma japonicum and its intermediate host, Oncomelania hupensis quadrasi, in freshwater from Ekiran village, Alangalang, Leyte Province, Philippines. Field-adaptable assay using environmental DNA (eDNA) was evaluated at 30 sites across four surveys from July 2023 to March 2024. The mLAMP-LFA demonstrated limits of detection from 57.2 to 194.9 copies per reaction, with 95% CIs of 7.7-427.3 to 35.2-1,077.9 copies. No cross-reactivity with non-target species observed. Compared with traditional malacological surveys, detection of S. japonicum rose from 1.7% to 18.5%, and O. h. quadrasi from 10.9% to 15.1%. Agreement with reference methods (Gwet's AC1) was substantial for S. japonicum (0.774-0.779) and moderate-to-substantial for O. h. quadrasi (0.538-0.766), both p<0.001. The approach offers rapid, field-ready, equipment-minimal multiplex eDNA surveillance to strengthen schistosomiasis monitoring and targeted control in resource-limited endemic settings.

articleSummary: Jinan, China: a retrospective study of 1,611 hospitalized children aged birth to under 18 with human metapneumovirus lower respiratory tract infection (2023–2025) found Mycoplasma pneumoniae co-detection markedly raised severe pneumonia risk. Overall, 301 children (18.7%) developed severe pneumonia and 36 (2.2%) required ICU care; infants 0–6 months had the highest ICU rate at 7.9%. In children over six years, atelectasis occurred in 22.4%, unilateral involvement 65.7%, and severe pneumonia 31.0%. Multivariable analysis identified atelectasis as the strongest predictor (adjusted OR 47.52), followed by chronic disease (OR 9.49), radiological consolidation (OR 6.82), fever (OR 3.29), and wheeze (OR 2.50). Mycoplasma pneumoniae co-detection nearly doubled odds of severe pneumonia (aOR 1.90). Higher absolute neutrophil counts and CRP linked to severity; higher monocyte counts (aOR 0.71) and broad bacterial co-detection (aOR 0.60) associated with lower odds. Age was not a predictor, though M. pneumoniae co-detection rose with age to 50% in >6 years.

articleHeadline: Brazilian Agroforests Harbor Surprising Mosquito Diversity and Disease
articleSummary: Three-year study (2022–2025) at Terra Boa Farm, Silva Jardim, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil documented 5,314 immature mosquitoes from 38 species. Culex dominated (53.8%), followed by Limatus (16.6%) and Wyeomyia (16.2%); five species—Cx. iridescens, Cx. pleuristriatus, Lim. durhamii, Wy. edwardsi, and Ae. albopictus—made up about 80% of captures. Natural habitats (bromeliads, bamboo internodes, peach palm bracts) yielded 4,175 specimens (78.6%) and 34 species, with 26 exclusive to natural sites; bromeliads produced 2,031 individuals from 22 species. Bamboo internodes were dominated by Cx. iridescens (72.4%) and harbored Toxorhynchites trichopygus larvae.
